books.title: Fog
books.art_why: Fog is a real weather event that photographs easily today.

pages.text: Fog looks like low clouds.
pages.brief: A wide outdoor view where a soft grey-white layer of fog lies low across the sky and land, sitting close to the ground and stretching far into the distance, looking just like clouds that have come down low.

pages.text: Fog looks white and spooky.
pages.brief: A thick white fog filling the whole outdoor scene, soft and pale, wrapping everything in a blank white haze that feels eerie and spooky, with shapes behind it faint and unclear.

pages.text: Fog can form out of small water drops.
pages.brief: A close, clear look at drifting mist made of many tiny water drops floating in the air, small and round, hanging together in a soft pale cloud of droplets.

pages.text: Fog can form out of tiny pieces of ice.
pages.brief: A close view of tiny pieces of ice, small bright crystals sparkling cold and white, floating and gathering in the chilled air as the beginnings of fog.

pages.text: Fog sometimes forms near water.
pages.brief: A calm lake or river with fog forming over the water, a soft white layer drifting above the surface and spreading out across the water into the air nearby.

pages.text: Fog sometimes forms near mountains.
pages.brief: Tall mountains with fog forming around them, pale grey-white mist settling along the slopes and between the peaks, softly hiding parts of the rocky mountain sides.

pages.text: Fog sometimes forms over wet land.
pages.brief: Wet, soggy land with fog forming above it, pale mist drifting low over the damp ground and shallow puddles, hanging in the air above the soft wet earth.

pages.text: Fog always forms near the ground.
pages.brief: An open outdoor scene showing fog lying right down near the ground, a low white layer hugging the surface while the air higher up stays clear above it.

pages.text: Fog always forms where air is still.
pages.brief: A still outdoor scene with no wind moving, fog hanging motionless in the quiet air, staying in one place in a soft white layer where the air does not stir.

pages.text: Fog always makes it hard to see.
pages.brief: An outdoor view filled with thick fog, so much white mist in the air that everything beyond it is blurred and hard to see, shapes fading away into the pale haze.

books.title: Insect Wings
books.art_why: The book shows real insects and their wings, which can be photographed.

pages.text: Insects have many kinds of wings.
pages.brief: A close-up nature photograph shows a group of insects with many different kinds of wings. Several insects are visible together, each with a different wing shape, pattern, or color. Their wings are spread or held at different angles so the variety is easy to see.

pages.text: Insects use their wings to fly.
pages.brief: A nature photograph shows insects using their wings to fly. Several insects are caught in midair with wings spread and moving. One insect rises above the others while the rest fly nearby, showing wings in motion against a soft outdoor background.

pages.text: This wasp has blue wings.
pages.brief: A close-up photograph shows a wasp with blue wings. The wasp is seen from the side, its blue wings spread out clearly. The thin wings catch the light, showing their color and shape while the wasp is shown in a natural setting.

pages.text: This grasshopper has green wings.
pages.brief: A close-up photograph shows a grasshopper with green wings. The grasshopper is seen from the side, with its green wings held along its body. The wing surface and edges are clear, and the insect stands out against a simple natural background.

pages.text: This moth has spotted wings.
pages.brief: A close-up photograph shows a moth with spotted wings. The moth is shown with its wings spread wide so the spots are easy to see. Its wings display a clear spotted pattern across the surface, and the moth is shown in a natural setting.

pages.text: This dragonfly has striped wings.
pages.brief: A close-up photograph shows a dragonfly with striped wings. The dragonfly is seen with its wings spread out so the stripes are visible. The stripes run across the clear wings, and the dragonfly is shown against a plain natural background.

pages.text: This ant has clear wings.
pages.brief: A close-up photograph shows an ant with clear wings. The ant is seen from the side, with its clear wings spread or held above its body. The wings look transparent, and the ant is shown in a natural setting with the wings easy to see.

pages.text: This butterfly has colorful wings.
pages.brief: A close-up photograph shows a butterfly with colorful wings. The butterfly is shown with its wings spread open, displaying bright colors and patterns. The colorful wings fill much of the view, and the butterfly is seen in a natural outdoor setting.

pages.text: Some insects have wing covers.
pages.brief: A close-up nature photograph shows insects that have wing covers. The insects are seen with wing covers folded over their backs, covering the wings underneath. The covers are clearly visible, and the insects are shown in a simple natural setting.

pages.text: Insects have many kinds of wings.
pages.brief: A close-up nature photograph shows a group of insects with many different kinds of wings. The insects are arranged together so their wings can be compared. Wing shapes, patterns, and colors vary from one insect to another, all shown clearly in the same view.

books.title: Imagine the Beach
books.art_why: A real beach and its sights, sounds, smells, textures and tastes exist today and can be photographed.

pages.text: Close your eyes.
pages.brief: A young child sits with eyes closed, hands still and face calm. The child is shown alone against a plain soft background, concentrating on the simple action of closing their eyes. No other objects are needed.

pages.text: Can you imagine the beach in your mind?
pages.brief: The same young child has a dreamy, thoughtful expression, imagining a beach inside their mind. A soft shape of a beach appears beside the child: sand, sea and sky. The child is not physically at the beach yet, only picturing it.

pages.text: What can you smell? Can you smell the salty air?
pages.brief: A child stands near the seashore, nose lifted, breathing in deeply. The air around the beach looks fresh and salty, with gentle sea mist. The child’s relaxed face shows they are noticing the smell of the salty air. Waves and sand are nearby.

pages.text: What can you hear? Can you hear the crashing waves?
pages.brief: A child stands on the beach, head tilted and listening. In front of them, waves crash and break into white foam. The child’s expression is attentive, focused on the sound of the crashing waves. Sand and open sky surround the scene.

pages.text: What can you see? Can you see the diving birds?
pages.brief: A child looks upward at the beach, shading their eyes. Above the water, birds dive down toward the sea. The child watches the diving birds with curiosity, seeing their wings and motion. Waves and sandy shore are visible below.

pages.text: What can you feel? Can you feel the rough sand?
pages.brief: A child kneels on the beach and touches the sand with open hands. The sand looks rough and textured. The child’s fingers press into it, feeling the rough sand. The sea and shoreline are nearby in the sunny beach setting.

pages.text: What can you taste? Can you taste the yummy ice cream?
pages.brief: A child at the beach holds a yummy ice cream cone and takes a bite. The ice cream looks colorful and delicious. The child’s happy face shows they can taste the yummy ice cream. Sand and sea are in the background.

pages.text: What else can you imagine at the beach? What do your mind and senses tell you?
pages.brief: A child stands on the beach with a thoughtful expression, looking around and using their senses. The beach stretches out with sand, waves and sky. The child seems to wonder what else can be imagined at the beach, with mind and senses working together.

books.title: River Otters
books.art_why: River otters are real animals living today, so real photographs are possible and best.

pages.text: River otters are amazing animals.
pages.brief: A river otter stands on a wet rock at the edge of a river, sleek brown body turned toward the reader, whiskers and small ears clear. Water flows behind it and green banks frame the scene, showing one real otter in its natural riverside home.

pages.text: All river otters live near water.
pages.brief: A river otter slips through shallow water close to a muddy bank, only its head and long back above the surface. Reeds and wet stones line the shore behind it, showing the otter right beside the water where it lives.

pages.text: All river otters have long, thin bodies.
pages.brief: A river otter stretches out along a log beside the river, its long, thin body shown from nose to tail in one clear line. Short fur, small head and tapering tail are visible as it rests in the open.

pages.text: All river otters have short legs.
pages.brief: A river otter walks on a sandy riverbank, seen from the side so its four short legs and low belly are easy to see. The little legs carry its long body over wet sand near the water's edge.

pages.text: All river otters have thick, warm fur.
pages.brief: A close view of a river otter's thick brown fur, damp and glossy, as the animal turns on a riverside rock. Individual hairs and the dense coat are visible across its back and neck, warm and dry-looking in the open air.

pages.text: All river otters are good at swimming.
pages.brief: A river otter swims strongly across a river, body level and tail sweeping behind it, paws tucked close. Ripples spread around its head and back as it moves through the open water under daylight.

pages.text: All river otters are good at holding their breath.
pages.brief: A river otter dives below the surface, mouth closed and eyes open, holding its breath underwater. Its body curves down through the green water past stones on the riverbed, with no air bubbles escaping.

pages.text: All river otters are good at catching food.
pages.brief: A river otter surfaces with food held firmly in its front paws and mouth, chewing near a flat rock at the water's edge. Its wet head and shoulders rise above the river as it feeds.

pages.text: All river otters are good at playing together.
pages.brief: Two river otters tumble and chase each other on a muddy riverbank, one rolling on its back while the other climbs over it. Both are close together, playing in the open beside the water.

pages.text: River otters are special animals. All river otters are good at being river otters.
pages.brief: A river otter sits upright on a riverside rock, front paws lifted, looking straight out over the water. Wet fur, whiskers and bright eyes are clear, showing one calm otter in its river home.

books.title: Bubbles
books.art_why: Bubbles are real, everyday objects that can be photographed.

pages.text: Bubbles are round pockets of air inside a material. People make bubbles with many things.
pages.brief: A close-up of a large round pocket of air trapped inside a clear material, shown as a perfect circle. A person's hands are visible nearby, making several round bubbles that drift softly in the air.

pages.text: People make bubbles with soap.
pages.brief: A close-up view of a child's hands covered in white soapy lather rub a bar of soap together. Small round soap bubbles form between the fingers and rise from the foam, filling the space around the hands.

pages.text: People make bubbles while chewing gum.
pages.brief: A young child sits outdoors on a sunny day and chews bubble gum happily. A large pink bubble grows from the child's mouth, round and shiny, with a few smaller bubbles floating in the air nearby.

pages.text: People make bubbles in milk.
pages.brief: A close-up of a tall glass of fresh white milk. Round bubbles sit on the surface of the milk and along the inside of the glass near the top, clearly visible as small pockets of air.

pages.text: People make bubbles under water.
pages.brief: A person swims underwater with their mouth open, blowing a stream of round bubbles. The bubbles rise gently toward the surface through bright clear blue water, while the swimmer's face and hands are visible nearby.

pages.text: Some bubbles are colorful.
pages.brief: A single large soap bubble fills the frame, its very thin surface shining with bright bands of pink, green, blue and yellow. Soft light reflects off the colorful film, making the round bubble glow softly.

pages.text: Some bubbles stick together.
pages.brief: A close-up of a cluster of round soap bubbles pressed together, sharing flat walls where they meet. The bubbles form a joined group, some large and some small, floating gently in a bright, clear space.

pages.text: Some bubbles float away.
pages.brief: Several round soap bubbles drift slowly upward into a high clear blue sky, carried by a gentle breeze. Below them, a child's hand releases more small bubbles that float away toward soft white clouds.

pages.text: Some bubbles are in solids.
pages.brief: A close-up shows a smooth solid block of clear material holding several round bubbles trapped inside it. The tiny air pockets sit still within the solid, visible clearly as perfect circles near the center.

pages.text: Bubbles hold air. Some bubbles hold people, too!
pages.brief: A smiling person sits inside a giant clear bubble, their face and hands pressed against the round wall. Beside them, a small clear bubble holds a pocket of air, showing how bubbles hold air too.

books.title: Cranberries
books.art_why: Cranberries, bogs and the foods made from them all exist today and can be photographed.

pages.text: Cranberries are fruits. They grow in bogs.
pages.brief: A wide view of a low, wet cranberry bog with shallow water between banks of small green shrubs. Tiny round red cranberries sit among the leaves and float at the water's surface, showing that these fruits grow in bogs.

pages.text: Cranberries are fruits. They grow on vines.
pages.brief: A close look at cranberry vines trailing low across sandy ground, thin stems and small glossy leaves tangled together. Several small red cranberries hang from the vines, making clear that the fruit grows on vines rather than on tall trees.

pages.text: Cranberries are fruits. They grow pink flowers.
pages.brief: An extreme close-up of a cranberry vine in bloom, with small pink flowers opening on the stems among narrow green leaves. The petals are curled back and pale pink, showing the flowers that come before the berries on these low-growing plants.

pages.text: Cranberries are fruits. They grow slowly.
pages.brief: The same cranberry vines seen over time in one frame: tight green buds, then small pale green berries, then berries turning pink and finally deep red. The berries sit close to the ground on the vines, showing how slowly the fruit grows and ripens.

pages.text: Cranberries taste tart. People eat them fresh.
pages.brief: A person's hand lifting a handful of firm, bright red fresh cranberries from a bowl on a kitchen table, with a few berries scattered nearby. The face is out of frame as the person pops one into their mouth, eating the cranberries fresh.

pages.text: Cranberries taste tart. People eat them dried.
pages.brief: A small bowl of dried cranberries, wrinkled and dark red, on a wooden surface beside a scatter of the dried fruit. A hand reaches in and lifts a few, showing people eating cranberries dried as a sweet, chewy snack.

pages.text: Cranberries taste tart. People eat them as jam.
pages.brief: A glass jar of dark red cranberry jam, open with a spoon inside, next to a slice of bread spread thickly with the jam. Whole berries show in the glossy jam, showing cranberries eaten as jam.

pages.text: Cranberries taste tart. People eat them as sauce.
pages.brief: A white bowl of smooth dark red cranberry sauce on a set table, a spoon resting in it and a small pool of sauce on the plate beside it. There are no people, just the sauce ready to be eaten with a meal.

books.title: Reindeer Are Real
books.art_why: Reindeer are real animals living today, so real photographs fit.

pages.text: Did you know that reindeer are real? Well, they are.
pages.brief: A reindeer stands in open tundra with a cold sky behind it, its breath visible in the air. Its antlers and thick coat are clearly visible as it looks toward the viewer, a real animal in its natural northern habitat.

pages.text: Reindeer sometimes pull sleds.
pages.brief: A reindeer wearing a harness pulls a wooden sled across flat snow. The sled trails behind on the white ground, and the reindeer leans forward as it walks, moving steadily over the snowy landscape under a pale winter sky.

pages.text: Reindeer sometimes dig for food.
pages.brief: A reindeer stands in deep snow with its head down, front hooves pawing at the white surface to uncover food beneath. A small hollow in the snow shows where it has dug, and the animal's breath fogs the cold air.

pages.text: Reindeer sometimes weigh a lot.
pages.brief: A large, sturdy reindeer stands broadside in a snowy field, its heavy body and thick neck filling much of the frame. Its strong legs and solid build are clear as it stands calmly on the flat white ground.

pages.text: Reindeer sometimes swim.
pages.brief: A reindeer swims through dark water with its head and antlers above the surface, legs moving beneath. Ripples spread around its neck as it crosses the river, cold banks visible in the background under an overcast sky.

pages.text: Reindeer sometimes travel many miles.
pages.brief: A line of reindeer walks nose to tail across a wide, open landscape of snow and low hills, stretching far into the distance. Their bodies are small against the vast ground as the herd travels steadily forward.

pages.text: All reindeer have thick fur.
pages.brief: A close view of a reindeer's thick coat, showing dense, shaggy fur across its neck and shoulder. The long winter hairs lie in layers over the animal's body, and part of its head and ear are visible at the edge of the frame.

pages.text: All reindeer eat only plants.
pages.brief: A reindeer stands on a grassy tundra slope with its head lowered, nibbling green plants and low leaves. More low vegetation spreads across the ground around its hooves, and soft daylight falls on its back and antlers.

pages.text: All reindeer can walk on ice.
pages.brief: A reindeer walks across a smooth sheet of ice, one hoof lifted mid-step. Its legs are steady on the slippery pale surface, and snowy ground edges the frozen area beneath a clear, cold sky.

pages.text: All reindeer can walk the day they are born.
pages.brief: A tiny newborn reindeer calf stands on wobbly legs beside an adult on open snowy ground. The calf's coat is dry and soft, and it holds itself upright on the snow, only just born and already standing.

books.title: How Do They Swim?
books.art_why: All the animals shown are real living animals that can be photographed today.

pages.text: Fish can swim. They use their fins and tails to swim.
pages.brief: Several fish of different sizes swim through clear water, their fins spread out to the sides and their tails curved as they push forward. Some swim near the surface, others a little deeper, all moving through the same open water with fins and tails doing the work.

pages.text: Ducks can swim. They use their feet to swim.
pages.brief: A duck swims across a pond, body sitting low on the water. Below the surface its webbed feet paddle back and forth, pushing the water behind it. Ripples spread out from the duck as it moves steadily forward across the pond.

pages.text: Beavers can swim. They use their feet and tails to swim.
pages.brief: A beaver swims through calm water, its big flat tail trailing behind and its dark feet kicking underwater. The tail sweeps from side to side as the beaver moves forward, its head above the surface and its body gliding along just beneath.

pages.text: Turtles can swim. They use their feet or flippers to swim.
pages.brief: A turtle swims through open water, front limbs stretched out and stroking, back limbs steering. One turtle uses sturdy feet, another uses long flippers, each pushing the water to move itself slowly forward past the viewer.

pages.text: Otters can swim. They use their feet and tails to swim.
pages.brief: An otter swims on its back through still water, feet paddling and thick tail sweeping behind it. Its body stays low and sleek in the water as the tail and feet work together to push the otter along.

pages.text: Bears can swim. They use their paws to swim.
pages.brief: A bear wades into a river and swims, head up and big paws reaching forward and pulling back through the water. The paws push down and back with each stroke, moving the heavy body steadily across the river.

pages.text: Seals can swim. They use their flippers to swim.
pages.brief: A seal glides through cold blue water, front flippers beating up and down like wings while the back flippers steer behind. Its smooth body slips forward easily as the flippers push the water away on each stroke.

pages.text: Snakes can swim. They use their bodies to swim.
pages.brief: A snake swims across the surface of the water, its long body bending in wide curves from side to side. Each curve pushes the water behind it, sending the snake forward in a smooth rippling line.

books.title: Community Helpers
books.art_why: Community helpers are real people doing real jobs today, so photographs are the right match.

pages.text: Who are the helpers in our community? Let us meet some of them.
pages.brief: A sunny neighbourhood street with a school, a bakery and a small park along the sidewalk. Several grown-ups are out and about: one walks with a bag, another sweeps a step, a third waves from a doorway. Children watch from a front yard, looking curious about the people they see around them every day.

pages.text: This is a teacher. She is an important helper. She lives in our community.
pages.brief: A woman teacher stands at the front of a bright classroom beside a low bookshelf and a chalkboard. She holds an open picture book and leans down toward a small group of children sitting on a rug, all looking up at her. Windows show a neighbourhood street outside.

pages.text: This is a trash collector. He is an important helper. He lives in our community.
pages.brief: A man in a bright safety vest and work gloves lifts a rubbish bin into the back of a rubbish truck on a quiet residential street. The truck's hopper is open, and bins line the kerb beside trimmed hedges and a low fence. Morning light falls across the pavement.

pages.text: This is a baker. He is an important helper. He lives in our community.
pages.brief: A baker in a white apron and cap stands behind a warm bakery counter, sliding a tray of round loaves from the oven with thick mitts. Bread rolls and a crusty loaf cool on the counter beside him. Shelves of flour sacks and a window onto the street are behind him.

pages.text: This is a construction worker. She is an important helper. She lives in our community.
pages.brief: A woman construction worker in a hard hat, safety vest and boots stands on a building site, one hand steadying a wooden beam while a crane hook hangs nearby. Stacked bricks, a ladder and partly built walls surround her. Loose soil and scattered tools lie at her feet.

pages.text: This is a firefighter. He is an important helper. He lives in our community.
pages.brief: A firefighter in a helmet, heavy coat and boots stands beside a red fire engine at the station, holding a coiled hose. The engine's lights and ladder are visible, and turnout gear hangs on the wall behind. The wide station door is open to a sunny street.

pages.text: This is a doctor. She is an important helper. She lives in our community.
pages.brief: A woman doctor in a white coat with a stethoscope around her neck stands in a bright clinic room, smiling as she holds a clipboard. An examination table with a folded blanket, a small sink and a shelf of supplies are behind her. A window lets in daylight.

pages.text: This is a service dog. She is an important helper, too.
pages.brief: A service dog with a harness and a calm, alert face sits beside a person's legs on a pavement in the community. The dog's leash is held loosely, and the pair waits near a crossing with shops and trees behind them. The dog looks ready and steady.

books.title: Where Animals Live
books.art_why: Real animals and their habitats can be photographed.

pages.text: Animals live in many different places. Some live above the ground. Some live in the ground. Some live on the ground. Some live in the water. This bird lives in the trees. The monkey lives in the trees, too.
pages.brief: A bird sits among the branches of a tree, and a monkey also sits in the trees nearby. The tree scene shows the two animals living above the ground, with leaves and branches around them.

pages.text: This frog lives in a pond. The turtle lives in a pond, too. This prairie dog lives in a burrow. The woodchuck lives in a burrow, too.
pages.brief: A frog sits in a pond, and a turtle also rests in the pond water. Nearby, a prairie dog stands at a burrow in the ground, and a woodchuck is at another burrow. The two burrows show animals living in the ground.

pages.text: These bats live in a cave. This bear lives in a cave, too. This deer lives in the woods. The fox lives in the woods, too.
pages.brief: Bats hang in a cave, and a bear also rests inside the cave. Outside, a deer stands among the trees in the woods, and a fox is in the woods nearby. The cave and woods are places where these animals live.

pages.text: This octopus lives in the ocean. The whale lives in the ocean, too. Mandy and Michael live in a house. People are animals, too.
pages.brief: An octopus swims in the ocean, and a whale also swims in the ocean water. On land, Mandy and Michael stand together in a house. They are people, and people are animals, too. The house is their place to live.

books.title: The Team
books.art_why: Baseball teams, players, and games exist in the real world, so photographs suit the book.

pages.text: Teams have players. A baseball team has nine players. Each player is important. The pitcher is very important. She pitches the ball to the batter.
pages.brief: A baseball team of nine players is shown on a baseball field. In the foreground, a female pitcher throws the ball toward a batter waiting nearby. Teammates watch from behind. The pitcher and batter are clearly shown as important parts of the team.

pages.text: The batter is very important. He hits the ball the pitcher pitches. The catcher is very important. He catches the ball the pitcher pitches.
pages.brief: A male batter hits the ball pitched to him on the baseball field. Behind the batter, a male catcher crouches with his glove raised, ready to catch a pitch. Both players are clearly shown as important parts of the team.

pages.text: The infielder is very important. She catches the ball the batter hits. The outfielder is very important. He catches the ball the batter hits.
pages.brief: A female infielder catches a ball hit by the batter, glove out and eyes on the ball. Nearby, a male outfielder also catches a batted ball, moving with his glove raised. Both stand on the baseball field, showing important fielding positions.

pages.text: All the players are important. To win, a team needs each player. Baseball is a team sport. Players play together to win.
pages.brief: All nine baseball players gather together on a baseball field, standing as one team. They show that every player matters. The group plays together, with each player supporting the others, showing how a baseball team works together to win.

books.title: Clouds
books.art_why: Clouds are real natural phenomena that can be photographed.

pages.text: Big white clouds fill the blue sky. What do you see in the clouds? Look at the puffy clouds. I see a snowman. What do you see?
pages.brief: In a wide blue sky, big white clouds fill the view. Among the puffy clouds, one cloud is clearly shaped like a snowman, with a round head, round body, and soft edges. The clouds float high above.

pages.text: Look at the jumbo clouds. A whale is what I see. What do you see? Look at the round clouds. I see a creamy pie. What do you see?
pages.brief: High in the blue sky, a jumbo cloud stretches into the shape of a whale, with a broad back and tail. Nearby, round clouds form a creamy pie with a soft, curved crust. Both cloud shapes float together.

pages.text: Do you see the fuzzy clouds? A sheep is what I see. Do you see it, too? Look at the very tall clouds. I see a mountain. Can you see the mountain?
pages.brief: In the blue sky, fuzzy clouds form the shape of a woolly sheep. Above and beside it, very tall clouds rise like a mountain, with a high peak and sloping sides. The cloud shapes stand out clearly.

pages.text: Look at the darker clouds. I see a thick blanket. What do you see? It’s starting to rain. Let’s go inside.
pages.brief: Darker clouds spread across the sky like a thick blanket, heavy and gray. The first raindrops begin to fall below them. The bright blue sky has faded, and the clouds look low and close overhead.

books.title: Senses
books.art_why: A child's senses, garden birds, bees, flowers and a real caterpillar are everyday things a camera can photograph.

pages.text: I like to learn about things. How do I learn about things? I use my five senses. I use my eyes to see. I see birds and bees.
pages.brief: A young child stands outdoors in the daytime with eyes wide open, looking up at small birds flying past and bees hovering nearby. The child's face is turned toward the birds and the bees, showing how the child uses eyes to see and learn about things.

pages.text: I use my ears to hear. I hear birds singing. I hear bees buzzing. I use my nose to smell. I smell pretty flowers.
pages.brief: The same child tilts an ear toward birds singing with open beaks and bees buzzing around, then leans in close to sniff a cluster of pretty flowers. Birds perch nearby and bees hover in the air while the child's nose touches the bright petals.

pages.text: I use my fingers to touch. I touch the fuzzy caterpillar. I use my tongue to taste. I taste sweet berries.
pages.brief: The child's fingers gently touch a fuzzy caterpillar crawling on a green leaf, feeling its soft bristles. Close by, the child's tongue touches a few sweet berries, tasting them, with more berries resting nearby within reach.

pages.text: I like to go to my garden. I use my five senses. I use them to see and hear. I use them to smell and taste. I use them to touch. I learn a lot from my senses.
pages.brief: The child stands happily in a garden full of flowers and berries, looking at birds and bees, listening to their sounds, smelling the flowers, tasting berries and touching leaves, using all five senses at once to learn a lot.

books.title: Caretakers
books.art_why: All the caretakers are real people at work today, so photographs fit.

pages.text: Caretakers take care of things. There are many kinds of caretakers. This farmer is a caretaker. She takes care of farms.
pages.brief: A woman farmer in work clothes and boots stands in a farmyard, holding a bucket and feeding animals in a pen behind her. Fenced fields and a barn spread out around her as she goes about her daily work taking care of the farm.

pages.text: This babysitter is a caretaker. He takes care of children. This road worker is a caretaker. She takes care of the roads.
pages.brief: A young man babysitting sits on the floor with two small children, playing with toys and smiling. Below him, a woman road worker in a hi-vis vest and hard hat kneels on a street, repairing the road surface with tools beside her.

pages.text: This vet is a caretaker. He takes care of animals. This doctor is a caretaker. She takes care of people.
pages.brief: A male vet in a clinic holds a small dog gently on an examination table, checking it over. Next to him, a woman doctor in a white coat with a stethoscope stands in a bright hospital room, talking kindly with a patient.

pages.text: This dentist is a caretaker. He takes care of teeth. These firefighters and teachers are caretakers. They take care of people, too.
pages.brief: A dentist in a mask and gloves leans over a patient in a dental chair, looking closely at the patient's teeth with a small mirror. Beside them, firefighters in helmets and teachers in a classroom both stand with the people they look after.

books.title: Where Plants Grow
books.art_why: Plants and their growing places are real-world subjects that can be photographed.

pages.text: Plants grow in many places. They can grow outside. They can grow inside, too. Most plants grow in soil.
pages.brief: A wide view shows plants growing in many places: several plants outdoors, several plants inside a room, and most plants standing in dark soil. Green leaves and stems are visible on the plants, with both the outdoor and indoor areas shown.

pages.text: Some plants grow in pots. There is soil inside the pots. Some plants grow in sand.
pages.brief: Several plants grow in pots, and dark soil is visible inside the pots. Nearby, other plants grow in a patch of sand, with their stems and leaves rising from the sandy ground. The pots and the sandy area are shown side by side.

pages.text: Some plants grow in water. Some plants grow on rocks.
pages.brief: Some plants grow in water, with stems and leaves rising from the water. Other plants grow on rocks, their roots and leaves clinging to the rocky surface. The water and the rocks are both shown clearly in the same outdoor view.

pages.text: Some plants even grow on other plants. Plants need three things to grow. They need water, air, and sunlight.
pages.brief: Some plants grow on other plants, with their leaves and stems resting on a larger plant. Plants are also shown with water nearby and sunlight falling on them, while open air surrounds them. The scene shows what plants need to grow.

books.title: Who Runs Faster?
books.art_why: Real animals and a child exist today, so photographs are possible.

pages.text: This is a tortoise. A squirrel can run faster than a tortoise. This is a squirrel. A girl can run faster than a squirrel.
pages.brief: A tortoise walks slowly on open ground. Beside it, a squirrel dashes forward. A young girl runs past the squirrel, arms out for balance. The three are shown outdoors in a simple natural setting, with the tortoise plodding, the squirrel scampering, and the girl running.

pages.text: This is a girl. A giraffe can run faster than a girl. This is a giraffe. A zebra can run faster than a giraffe.
pages.brief: A young girl runs across open ground. Nearby, a tall giraffe strides along, long neck high. A zebra gallops close by, stripes clearly visible. The scene is outdoors with the girl running, the giraffe walking, and the zebra running in a simple natural setting.

pages.text: This is a zebra. A lion can run faster than a zebra. This is a lion. An antelope can run faster than a lion.
pages.brief: A zebra gallops across open ground, stripes stark. A lion runs nearby, mane flowing, body low. An antelope sprints ahead, slender legs stretched. All three are outdoors in a simple natural setting, with the zebra running, the lion moving forward, and the antelope bounding.

pages.text: This is an antelope. A cheetah can run faster than an antelope. This is a cheetah. Nothing can run faster than a cheetah.
pages.brief: An antelope bounds across open ground, horns small and legs long. A cheetah sprints beside it, spotted coat stretched low, tail trailing. The cheetah is shown as the fastest animal, with the antelope running and the cheetah racing forward in a simple outdoor setting.

books.title: The Busy Pond
books.art_why: A real pond with real plants and animals exists today, so photographs fit best.

pages.text: I see water when I go to the pond. I can see land all around the water.
pages.brief: A wide view of a pond filled with still water, with land stretching all around the water's edge. Low grassy ground and open shoreline surround the pond on every side, showing where the water meets the land under daylight.

pages.text: I see cattails when I go to the pond. They are very tall.
pages.brief: Tall cattails grow close together at the edge of the pond, their long stems rising well above the surrounding plants. The brown seed heads stand high against the sky, with water and shoreline visible behind the slender, upright stems.

pages.text: I see lily pads when I go to the pond. They are very round.
pages.brief: Round lily pads float on the calm surface of the pond, spread out across the water. Their circular green shapes rest flat on top of the water, with open pond surface visible between them and soft ripples around their edges.

pages.text: I see frogs when I go to the pond. They sit on the lily pads.
pages.brief: Frogs sit on top of the floating lily pads in the pond. Their small bodies rest on the round green leaves as the pads float on the water, with several frogs spaced across the pond surface in the daylight.

pages.text: I see turtles when I go to the pond. They sit on a log.
pages.brief: Turtles sit together on a fallen log at the pond, their shells resting on the bark. The log lies at the water's edge while the turtles stay in place on top of it, with pond water visible beside the wood.

pages.text: I see ducks when I go to the pond. They swim on the water.
pages.brief: Ducks swim across the open water of the pond, their bodies moving along the surface. Several ducks paddle through the calm water, leaving small ripples behind them as they travel together across the pond in daylight.

pages.text: I see fish when I go to the pond. They swim in the water.
pages.brief: Fish swim beneath the surface of the pond water, their bodies moving through the clear water. They are seen underwater as they glide along, with the pond surrounding them and no land or sky in view.

pages.text: I see many things when I go to the pond. The pond is a busy place.
pages.brief: A broad view of the busy pond shows water, land around the edge, tall cattails, round lily pads, frogs on the pads, turtles on a log, ducks swimming and fish in the water. Many living things fill the pond scene.
